entry.title: Agentic RAG in 65 lines: LangGraph 1.2, Claude and Redis 8 vector sets

link.title: Agentic RAG in 65 lines: LangGraph 1.2, Claude and Redis 8 vector sets

entry.content:
At the end of this post you have one Python file, 65 lines of code, that turns any Markdown document into a chat assistant. It searches the document before answering, cites the passages it used as [n], and remembers what you tell it about yourself across turns. The model plans the searches; Redis holds the passages, the vectors and the memory.

   
Agent LangGraph 1.2 via langchain.agents.create_agent (LangChain 1.4)
Model Claude Opus 5.5 (anthropic:claude-opus-5-5), any tool-calling chat model works
Storage Beanis 0.3 on Redis 8: documents in hashes, embeddings in a native vector set
Embeddings fastembed BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, 384 dimensions, local CPU, no API key
Requirements Python 3.10+, Redis 8.0+ (docker run -p 6379:6379 redis:8 or brew install redis), ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

Redis 8 ships vector sets (VADD, VSIM) in the core server. That is what makes this setup small: no Redis Stack, no RediSearch index to create, no separate vector database. Beanis stores each document as a hash and puts its embedding in a vector set, together with the document’s short fields so you can filter a search.

The whole program

pip install "beanis>=0.3" "langchain>=1.4" langchain-anthropic fastembed

# rag.py
import asyncio
import re
import urllib.request
from typing import List

from fastembed import TextEmbedding
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
from redis.asyncio import Redis
from typing_extensions import Annotated

from beanis import Document, IndexedField, Memory, VectorField, init_beanis

DOCS = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andreim14/beanis/main/README.md"
embedder = TextEmbedding("BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5")  # 384 dims, runs on CPU


def embed(text: str) -> List[float]:
    return next(iter(embedder.embed([text]))).tolist()


class Chunk(Document):
    text: str
    source: Annotated[str, IndexedField()]
    embedding: Annotated[List[float], VectorField(dimensions=384)]


def split(markdown: str, source: str):
    for section in re.split(r"\n(?=#{1,3} )", markdown):
        if len(section.strip()) > 80:
            text = section.strip()[:2000]
            yield Chunk(text=text, source=source, embedding=embed(text))


@tool
async def search_docs(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the documentation. Returns numbered passages; cite them as [n]."""
    hits = await Chunk.vector_search(embed(query), k=4)
    return "\n\n".join(f"[{i}] {c.text}" for i, (c, _) in enumerate(hits, 1))


async def build_agent(model, redis):
    await init_beanis(database=redis, document_models=[Chunk])
    await Chunk.delete_all()
    readme = urllib.request.urlopen(DOCS).read().decode()
    await Chunk.insert_many(split(readme, "beanis/README.md"))
    memory = Memory(redis, embed=embed, namespace="docs-bot")

    @tool
    async def remember(fact: str) -> str:
        """Save a lasting fact or preference about the user."""
        await memory.remember(fact, user_id="me")
        return "saved"

    @tool
    async def recall(query: str) -> str:
        """Look up what you know about the user."""
        return "\n".join(m.text for m, _ in await memory.recall(query, user_id="me"))

    return create_agent(
        model,
        tools=[search_docs, remember, recall],
        system_prompt="Answer questions about Beanis using search_docs and cite "
        "passages as [n]. Say so when the docs do not cover something. Use "
        "recall for the user's preferences and remember for new ones.",
        checkpointer=InMemorySaver(),  # keeps the conversation per thread_id
    )


async def main():
    agent = await build_agent(
        init_chat_model("anthropic:claude-opus-5-5"), Redis(decode_responses=True)
    )
    config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "cli"}}
    while question := input("\nyou> ").strip():
        result = await agent.ainvoke(
            {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": question}]}, config
        )
        print("bot>", result["messages"][-1].content)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

Run it with python rag.py and ask about the document. Point DOCS at your own Markdown to make it your assistant.

How it works

Agentic, not a fixed pipeline. Classic RAG always retrieves once, then answers. Here retrieval is a tool. The model can search twice with different wording, skip searching for small talk, or look up your preferences first. create_agent builds the LangGraph loop for you (model, then tools, then model, until it answers), and InMemorySaver keeps each conversation by thread_id. Swap it for a persistent checkpointer when you deploy.

Storage in one class. Chunk is a Pydantic model. IndexedField puts source in a Redis set for exact lookups. VectorField(dimensions=384) stores the embedding in a Redis 8 vector set (HNSW, cosine, int8 quantization by default). Chunk.vector_search(vector, k=4) returns (chunk, score) pairs, best first, with the score between 0 and 1.

Filters for free. Every short field of a document travels with its vector, so with several sources you can narrow the search inside the same call:

await Chunk.vector_search(embed(query), k=4, filter='.source == "beanis/README.md"')

Memory that survives the session. Memory keeps what the user said in Redis, scoped by namespace and user, and merges near-duplicates instead of piling up copies. The checkpointer remembers the current conversation; Memory remembers the user across conversations.

What a run looks like

I tested the file with a scripted stand-in model that makes the same tool calls Claude would, so the indexing, retrieval and memory run for real against Redis 8.10:

chunks indexed: 44

you> I deploy on Redis 8 in Docker
[remember] -> saved

you> How do I deploy?
[recall] -> I deploy on Redis 8 in Docker

The README splits into 44 sections; remember and recall round-trip through the vector set. With a real model, the final answer is written from those tool results.

Same memory, as an MCP server

If your agent is Claude Code, Claude Desktop or any MCP client, you do not need the memory code at all. Beanis ships it as an MCP server. In Claude Code, install the plugin (it needs uv and a Redis 8):

claude plugin marketplace add andreim14/beanis
claude plugin install beanis@beanis

Or register the server by hand, for any client:

pip install "beanis[mcp]"
claude mcp add beanis-memory --env REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/0 -- beanis-mcp

The client gets four tools: remember, recall, forget and recent, with local embeddings and no API key. The same memory is on the command line, with JSON output, for scripts and agents that prefer a shell:

beanis doctor                                  # is this Redis ready?
beanis memory remember "We deploy on Tuesdays" --kind decision
beanis memory recall "when do we deploy?"

Questions people ask

Do I need Redis Stack or RediSearch for vector search? Not any more. Redis 8.0+ has vector sets built in, and Beanis 0.3 uses them. Redis 7 and Valkey do not have them; Beanis tells you at startup instead of returning empty results.

Why fastembed instead of an embedding API? It runs locally on the CPU with a small ONNX model (bge-small, about 130 MB), so indexing costs nothing and works offline. Any function that turns text into a list of floats works: pass it as embed.

Can I use a model other than Claude? Yes. init_chat_model takes any provider LangChain supports, for example "openai:..." or "ollama:...", as long as the model supports tool calling.

How many documents can this handle? Vector sets use HNSW, so search stays fast as the set grows. The limits you will hit first are memory (with the default int8 quantization a 384-dimension vector is 384 bytes plus the HNSW graph links, and the text sits in the hash) and ingest speed, which is bound by the embedding model.

How do I keep the index fresh? Re-run the ingest with stable ids (for example Chunk(id=f"{source}#{n}", ...)). Saving a document with an existing id replaces it and updates its vector.

Links: Beanis on GitHub · PyPI · LangChain agents · Redis vector sets
entry.summary: A docs assistant that searches, cites its sources and remembers the user, in one 65-line Python file: LangGraph 1.2 create_agent, Claude Opus 5.5, Beanis 0.3 on Redis 8 vector sets (no Redis Stack) and local fastembed embeddings.

entry.title: Beanis: an async Redis ODM for Python with Pydantic models

link.title: Beanis: an async Redis ODM for Python with Pydantic models

entry.content:
Beanis is an open-source async object-document mapper (ODM) for Redis. You define Pydantic models, and Beanis stores them as Redis hashes, maintains secondary indexes and turns them back into typed objects. By the end of this post you will have a working model with validation, index queries and TTLs.

   
Package pip install beanis (0.2.0)
Code github.com/andreim14/beanis (Apache 2.0)
Docs andreim14.github.io/beanis
Requirements Python 3.9+, Pydantic (>=1.10,<3), redis-py 5+ async client, Redis 5+. No Redis modules for core features; vector search needs RediSearch (Redis Stack).

Minimal example

Start Redis (docker run -d -p 6379:6379 redis:7), then:

import asyncio
from typing import Optional

from redis.asyncio import Redis
from beanis import Document, Indexed, init_beanis


class Product(Document):
    name: str
    description: Optional[str] = None
    price: Indexed(float)          # sorted set index: range queries
    category: Indexed(str)         # set index: exact match
    stock: int = 0


async def main():
    client = Redis(host="localhost", port=6379, decode_responses=True)
    await init_beanis(database=client, document_models=[Product])

    product = Product(name="Tony's Chocolonely", price=5.95, category="chocolate", stock=100)
    await product.insert()

    found = await Product.get(product.id)
    print(found.name, found.price)

    cheap = await Product.find(price__lte=10.0)
    chocolate = await Product.find(category="chocolate", price__gte=1.0)
    print(len(cheap), len(chocolate))

    await product.update(price=6.95, stock=150)
    print(await product.increment_field("stock", -1))  # atomic HINCRBY

    await product.delete_self()
    await client.close()


asyncio.run(main())

decode_responses=True is required: Beanis expects strings back from Redis, not bytes.

Why Beanis exists

Redis is fast, but the code around a hash is repetitive. Every read converts strings back to numbers, every nested object goes through json.dumps and json.loads, and every secondary index is a sorted set or set you update by hand:

raw = await redis.hgetall(f"Product:{product_id}")
product = {
    "name": raw["name"],
    "price": float(raw["price"]),
    "category": json.loads(raw["category"]),
}

With Beanis that becomes await Product.get(product_id), and you get a validated Product back.

I like Beanie, the MongoDB ODM. Beanis started as a fork of it and keeps its style (Pydantic models, init_* call, event hooks) on top of plain Redis commands. Compared with Redis OM, Beanis does not need the RedisJSON or RediSearch modules for documents, indexes or geo queries.

How Beanis stores a document in Redis

For Product with id abc:

Redis key Type Holds
Product:abc hash the fields; nested models, lists and dicts as JSON strings
all:Product sorted set every id, scored by insert time (used by all() and count())
idx:Product:price sorted set id scored by price (int and float fields)
idx:Product:category:chocolate set ids with that exact value (other indexed types)
idx:Product:location geo set ids by coordinates (GeoPoint fields)

The key prefix defaults to the class name. Set key_prefix in class Settings to change it.

How to query by index

find() takes keyword filters on indexed fields and returns a list. Several filters are combined with AND (set intersection).

await Product.find(category="chocolate")                # exact match on a set index
await Product.find(price__gte=10, price__lte=50)        # range on a sorted set index
await Product.find(category="chocolate", price__lte=5)  # both

Range operators work on int and float fields. Use __gte and __lte. Strings, booleans and dates are indexed for exact match only. Filtering on a field that is not indexed raises ValueError.

Indexes are written by insert(). In 0.2.0, insert_many() and update() write the hash only, so use insert() for documents you want to find by index.

For everything else there are id-based and scan-style helpers:

products = await Product.get_many([id1, id2, id3])   # pipelined, returns None for missing ids
page = await Product.all(skip=0, limit=20, sort_desc=True)
total = await Product.count()
exists = await Product.exists(id1)

How to validate data before it reaches Redis

Models are Pydantic models, so constraints are checked when you build the object:

from pydantic import Field, ValidationError
from beanis import Document, Indexed


class User(Document):
    username: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=20)
    age: int = Field(ge=13, le=120)
    score: Indexed(int) = 0


try:
    User(username="ab", age=200)
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e)  # two errors, nothing written to Redis

Reads skip validation by default (model_construct), because the data came from your own writes. Set use_validation_on_fetch = True in Settings if you want reads validated too.

How to expire documents with TTL

await product.insert(ttl=3600)     # expires in one hour
await product.set_ttl(7200)
print(await product.get_ttl())
await product.persist()            # remove the expiry

You can also set default_ttl in Settings.

How to run code before or after insert, update, delete

from beanis import Document, before_event, after_event, Insert, Update


class Order(Document):
    total: float
    status: str = "pending"

    @before_event(Insert)
    async def check_total(self):
        if self.total < 0:
            raise ValueError("total cannot be negative")

    @after_event(Update)
    async def log_update(self):
        print(f"order {self.id} updated")

How to store custom types (NumPy, your own classes)

NumPy arrays and PyTorch tensors are registered automatically when those libraries are installed. For your own types, register an encoder and decoder that convert to and from a string:

from dataclasses import dataclass
from beanis import register_type


@dataclass
class Money:
    amount: str
    currency: str


register_type(
    Money,
    encoder=lambda m: f"{m.amount}:{m.currency}",
    decoder=lambda s: Money(*s.split(":")),
)

register_encoder(type_) and register_decoder(type_) do the same as decorators.

Geo and vector fields

Two index types go beyond sets and sorted sets:

  • GeoPoint with an index uses GEOADD and GEORADIUS. See the restaurant finder tutorial.
  • VectorField(dimensions=...) creates a RediSearch HNSW index at init_beanis time. This one needs Redis Stack. See the RAG tutorial.

Performance

The README reports about 8% overhead over plain redis-py for get-by-id. The benchmark script behind that number is not in the repo, so treat it as indicative. The design choices that keep reads cheap are visible in the source: msgspec for JSON parsing, model_construct() instead of full validation on reads, and pipelines for insert_many, get_many and delete_many.

When not to use Beanis

  • Plain key-value caching, where a GET/SET is all you need.
  • You need full-text search or JSON path queries: use RediSearch and RedisJSON directly, or Redis OM.
  • You need relations or aggregations. Beanis has neither (Beanie’s Link, aggregation pipelines and migrations were removed).

Questions people ask

What is the difference between Beanis and Redis OM? Redis OM relies on the RediSearch module for queries (and RedisJSON for JSON models). Beanis stores hashes and builds its indexes from plain sets, sorted sets and geo sets, so it runs on stock Redis.

Does Beanis work with Pydantic v2? Yes. The package declares pydantic>=1.10,<3, and the geo type uses Pydantic v2 validators.

Can I use Indexed[float] like in Beanie? No. In Beanis Indexed is a function: write Indexed(float), or Annotated[float, IndexedField()].

Is update() atomic? update(**fields) writes the given fields with one HSET. For counters use increment_field(), which is a single HINCRBY (or HINCRBYFLOAT for floats).

Which Python versions are supported? Python 3.9 and later, per the package metadata on PyPI.

Links

  • PyPI: pypi.org/project/beanis
  • GitHub: github.com/andreim14/beanis
  • Docs: andreim14.github.io/beanis
  • Examples: github.com/andreim14/beanis-examples
entry.summary: Beanis maps Pydantic models to Redis hashes, keeps secondary indexes for you and gives you a Beanie-style async API. Install, define a model, insert, query by index, set TTLs.
